# Frozen legacy user-level golden corpus (change 0322, Task B1)

These are **byte-exact snapshots of what the FINAL v0.9.2 Bash installer wrote**, frozen so the Go
`LegacyReproducer` (change 0311's third ownership proof, `inspect.go` `provenByLegacy`) can prove
that an on-disk artifact is an exact legacy install and adopt it instead of reporting an
ownership conflict. Every later Part-B task (B2–B7) derives its goldens from this corpus; when a
future live `internal/harness/*` renderer disagrees with a byte here, **the legacy capture wins** —
the reproducer proves *legacy ownership*, not current-render equality.

## Provenance — how these bytes were produced

- **Source of truth:** the clean v0.9.2 checkout at `/Users/homer/dev/docket-v0.9.2`.
- **Commit (`git -C /Users/homer/dev/docket-v0.9.2 rev-parse HEAD`):**
  `ca8251e8bc0a7944ece39dd750b1b159c978f2b3` — tag `v0.9.2`. Recorded verbatim in
  `_inputs/PROVENANCE-v0.9.2-HEAD.txt`.
- **Generators run:** that checkout's `sync-agents.sh` (agent definitions, Cursor dispatch rule,
  managed dispatch block). `link-skills.sh` was read but produces only source-linked skill
  directories, which are **out of this inventory** (see "link-skills.sh" below).
- **Capture method:** each pin shape was generated by running the v0.9.2 `sync-agents.sh` once under
  a fully sandboxed environment — `HOME=$sandbox DOCKET_HARNESS_ROOT=$sandbox`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
  unset — with a controlled `$sandbox/.config/docket/config.yml` (frozen at `_inputs/config-*.yml`).
  Nothing under the real `$HOME` was touched, and nothing in the v0.9.2 checkout was modified. The
  reference sidecar `agents/harness-defaults.yml` from v0.9.2 is frozen at
  `_inputs/harness-defaults.yml`. The whole corpus is regenerable with the guarded generator
  `TestCaptureLegacyCorpus` (`DOCKET_LEGACY_CAPTURE=1 go test ./internal/install -run
  TestCaptureLegacyCorpus`, optional `DOCKET_V092=<path>`); it rewrites only the generated files and
  preserves this README.

## The closed inventory (spec "Legacy adoption contract", lines 85–88)

Exactly three artifact shapes. Source-linked skill directories are 0311's separate link-identity
proof and are **not** here.

| # | Kind (`internal/install` Kind) | What | Where captured |
|---|--------------------------------|------|----------------|
| a | `KindFile` | Native user-level docket agent definitions `~/.<harness>/agents/docket-*.{md,toml}` | `<harness>/<shape>/agents/` |
| b | `KindFile` (regular file, **not** a symlink) | Cursor's docket dispatch rule `~/.cursor/rules/docket-dispatch.mdc` | `cursor/docket-dispatch.mdc` |
| c | `KindManagedBlock` (`BlockName == "dispatch"`) | The docket-managed dispatch-block **interior** inside harness instruction files (Claude `CLAUDE.md`, Codex/OpenCode `AGENTS.md`) | `dispatch-block/interior.md` (+ full `block.md`) |

## Harnesses × pin-shapes × kinds — what EXISTS and what is EMPTY

Harnesses captured: `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode` (the four v0.9.2 shipped harnesses with
a named emitter and a complete `harness-defaults.yml` block). Pin shapes: four (three named by the
spec + one realistic `default`; see below).

### Kind (a) — native agent definitions: EXISTS for every (harness × shape)

Two representative agents are frozen per (harness, shape), covering **both wrapper variants**:

- `docket-status` — **skill-bearing** (`skills: [docket-status, docket-convention]`): exercises the
  skills-preload preamble in the codex/cursor/opencode emitters.
- `docket-brainstorm-consultant` — **skill-less** (no `skills:` frontmatter — it is the *only*
  built-in that wraps no skill): exercises the no-preamble path.

The frontmatter/pin bytes for a given (harness, shape) are identical across all 16 built-in agents;
the other 14 differ **only in the agent body** (name/description/skills/body copied from
`agents/docket-*.md`). So the two captured agents fully represent the pin parameterisation; the 14
uncaptured agents are an **intentional empty category** (regenerate via the capture procedure if a
later task needs the full tree). File extension is `.toml` for `codex`, `.md` for the rest.

### Kind (b) — Cursor dispatch rule: EXISTS once; EMPTY for non-cursor harnesses

`cursor/docket-dispatch.mdc`. **Pin-invariant** — `assemble_dispatch_rule` splices static head +
run-gate + per-agent fragments and interpolates no model/effort. Verified byte-identical across all
four shapes at capture time, so it is stored once (not per shape). It is a **regular file** the
legacy installer wrote with `assemble_dispatch_rule > …/docket-dispatch.mdc` (confirm for B3:
`KindFile`, not `KindSymlink`). Claude/Codex/OpenCode emit no such rule → **empty category** for
those harnesses (Claude uses native `context: fork`; only Cursor needs the alwaysApply rule).

### Kind (c) — managed dispatch block: EXISTS once; harness-neutral and pin-invariant

`dispatch-block/interior.md` (the interior between the markers) and `dispatch-block/block.md` (the
full block including the `<!-- docket:dispatch:start … -->` / `<!-- docket:dispatch:end -->`
markers). **Pin-invariant AND harness-neutral:** `sync_dispatch_surfaces` writes the *same*
`assemble_agents_md_dispatch` output into every targeted instruction file, so the Claude `CLAUDE.md`
block and the Codex/OpenCode `AGENTS.md` block are byte-identical (in v0.9.2 the installer even
makes `CLAUDE.md` a symlink to `AGENTS.md`). Verified identical across all four shapes and across
`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` at capture time. Stored once.

Note for B4: the block carries **no model IDs** (machine-neutral by design). The Go proof compares
`normalizeInterior(on-disk interior) == normalizeInterior(reproducer output)` (`inspect.go`), which
trims one trailing newline and normalizes CRLF — so `interior.md`'s exact trailing newline is not
load-bearing. Also note provenance: the legacy installer wrote this block at **project/repo level**
(committed `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`), not into a user-level file — the user-level pass writes no
dispatch block. The reproducer's `KindManagedBlock` target is that instruction-file block.

## Pin shapes and the exact rendering parameterisation (for B2)

Each shape is the resolved-pin outcome fed to the v0.9.2 emitters. `AgentPins` in B2's
`LegacyInputs` are these **resolved** (model, effort) values.

| Shape | Global config (`_inputs/config-*.yml`) | Resolved (model, effort) for the two captured agents |
|-------|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `default` | no `agents:` block — pure `harness-defaults.yml` sidecar | **status:** claude=(`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`,`medium`), cursor=(`cursor-grok-4.5-low-fast`,`auto`), codex=(`gpt-5.6-luna`,`xhigh`), opencode=(`openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`,`low`). **brainstorm-consultant:** claude=(`claude-opus-5`,`medium`), cursor=(`cursor-grok-4.5-high`,`auto`), codex=(`gpt-5.6-sol`,`medium`), opencode=(`openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3`,`medium`) |
| `fully-pinned` | `agents.default.<pair> = { model: legacy-pinned-model, effort: high }` | both agents, **every harness**: (`legacy-pinned-model`, `high`) |
| `partially-pinned` | `{ model: legacy-pinned-model, effort: auto }` | (`legacy-pinned-model`, effort resolves **empty** — `auto` is the drop sentinel) |
| `unpinned` | `{ model: inherit, effort: auto }` | (`inherit`, empty) |

`default` is the **realistic** install a migrating user most likely had (real shipped IDs, varied
per harness/agent) — the tree B5/B6 seed. `fully-pinned`/`partially-pinned`/`unpinned` are
synthetic, override-driven, and **uniform** (identical pins for both agents on every harness) so
each drives one deterministic rendering branch. Model IDs in the synthetic shapes are arbitrary bare
scalars — the reproducer reproduces *bytes*, not realistic IDs.

### Per-harness emit rules the corpus proves (read the branches off the four shapes)

- **claude** (`emit`): `model: <m>` verbatim when `m` non-empty — **`inherit` passes through
  verbatim** (a real Claude Code frontmatter value, unlike the other harnesses); `effort: <e>` when
  `e` non-empty and `!= auto`. → default/fully = both lines; partial = model only; unpinned =
  `model: inherit` (no effort).
- **codex** (`emit_codex_toml`): `model = "<m>"` when `m` non-empty and `!= inherit`;
  `model_reasoning_effort = "<e>"` when `e` non-empty and `!= auto`, **independent of model**. →
  default/fully = both; partial = model only; unpinned = **no pin lines**.
- **cursor** (`emit_cursor_md`): `model: <m>` when `m` non-empty and `!= inherit`; append
  `[effort=<e>]` **only when a model is also present** and `e` non-empty and `!= auto`. → default =
  `model: <id>` (sidecar effort is `auto`); fully = `model: legacy-pinned-model[effort=high]` (the
  **effort-suffix** branch); partial = model only; unpinned = **no model line**.
- **opencode** (`emit_opencode_md`): `model: <m>` when `m` non-empty and `!= inherit`;
  `reasoningEffort: <e>` **only when a model is present** and `e` non-empty and `!= auto`; constant
  `mode: subagent` always. → default/fully = both; partial = model only; unpinned = `mode:
  subagent` only.

## Explicitly EMPTY categories (learning `frozen-corpus-covers-what-it-contains`)

- **codex/opencode "effort-only" (empty model + concrete effort):** not in the corpus. It is
  unreachable from these four shapes (an empty model here only ever comes from `inherit`, which is
  paired with `auto` effort). The v0.9.2 emitters *would* render it (codex would emit
  `model_reasoning_effort` with no `model`; opencode would **drop** the effort), but no golden bytes
  exist for it. B2/B7 must cover it by logic/mutation, not by a golden here.
- **cursor "effort with no model":** structurally impossible — the emitter drops effort when no
  model resolves. No fixture, by construction.
- **claude "truly unpinned" (no model line at all):** not reachable while the sidecar is complete
  (claude never normalizes a model to empty; `inherit` is emitted verbatim). The nearest capture is
  `unpinned` = `model: inherit`.
- **The 14 non-captured built-in agents** per (harness, shape): identical pin bytes to the captured
  pair; bodies differ only. Intentional — regenerate if needed.
- **Non-shipped harness tokens** (`agents`, `kiro`, `windsurf` from `DOCKET_GI_HARNESS_TOKENS`):
  no named emitter, no sidecar block → Claude-shaped/unpinned. Not in the reproducer inventory; not
  captured.

## link-skills.sh inventory (out of scope — recorded for completeness)

`link-skills.sh` creates **source-linked skill directories only**: for each `skills/<name>/` in the
docket checkout it makes an **absolute symlink** `~/.<harness>/skills/<name> -> <checkout>/skills/<name>`
into each *present* harness whose parent dir exists. Harness skill dirs it targets: `.claude/skills`,
`.codex/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.kiro/skills`, `.windsurf/skills`. It bakes no
model/effort and is idempotent (only creates missing links). These symlinked skill dirs are handled
by change 0311's **link-identity** proof (proof one/two, `provenByRecord`/link canonicalisation),
**not** by the frozen `LegacyReproducer`, so no skill-dir bytes are frozen here.

## `_inputs/` (capture inputs, not adoption goldens)

- `PROVENANCE-v0.9.2-HEAD.txt` — the frozen v0.9.2 commit.
- `config-<shape>.yml` — the exact global `config.yml` fed to `sync-agents.sh` for each shape.
- `harness-defaults.yml` — the v0.9.2 shipped sidecar (the resolution floor behind the `default`
  shape's pins). B2's own frozen template lives under `internal/install/legacydata/`, not here.
